topSignals.title: Trump personally engages Senate Majority Leader Thune on a companion bill to cut data-center electricity costs, as three competing Senate proposals now crowd the same lane.
topSignals.text: Trump told reporters Sept 18 "I'm talking to him about it, we'll see what happens" regarding Senate floor action after Republicans' unanimous-consent attempt to fast-track the House-passed Ratepayer Protection Act failed on Sept 17 (Sen. Heinrich's objection, already logged). Three distinct vehicles are now in play: the House's Ratepayer Protection Act (417-3, large-load cost-shift via state regulators), Sen. Van Hollen's separate "Power for the People Act" (S. 3682, directs states to create data-center-specific rate classes), and Senate Finance ranking member Wyden's August white paper proposing a gross-receipts excise tax on data centers (pre-2024 assets exempted) plus removal of Opportunity Zone/REIT tax benefits for new builds. The Senate is in session only a few more weeks before the Nov 3 midterm recess, raising the odds some version moves before year-end. For Dominic: multiple bills converging on the same "data centers should bear their own grid costs" logic reinforces the behind-the-meter SOFC case regardless of which specific text passes. U.S. News/Reuters | Route Fifty (Wyden proposal)

topSignals.title: Mizuho raises Bloom Energy price target 45% to $351 (from $242), citing stronger pricing power and higher long-term EBITDA margins, keeping its Outperform rating — ahead of Bloom's formal S&P 500 inclusion at Monday's (Sept 21) open.
topSignals.text: The note attributes the target increase to demand-driven pricing strength rather than a new contract or technical disclosure; no new commercial announcement accompanies it. Comes on top of the index-inclusion flow already driving the stock (+222% YTD, logged yesterday). Investing.com | Barchart

topSignals.title: Priority stacks Elcogen and Topsoe: third consecutive quiet day — no new announcements from either.
topSignals.text: Elcogen unchanged since the Sept 15 Shanghai HyEnergy supply agreement (elcoStack E3000 G2, ELCO I Tallinn at 360 MW/yr). Topsoe unchanged since the Sept 7 Uniper e-methanol FEED contract; SOEC-only Herning factory remains the flagship asset, SOFC/data-center pathway still deferred under the May 2026 roadmap review. Direct site checks (elcogen.com, topsoe.com/press-releases) confirm no new releases in the last 24-48h.

items.text: Elcogen (priority): No new news. Standing status unchanged — see Top Signal #3.
Topsoe (priority): No new news. Standing status unchanged — see Top Signal #3.
Ceres Power: No new stack/cell news; H1 2026 results still due before market open Wednesday Sept 23 (consensus loss ~$0.0644/share, revenue ~$34.75M) — unchanged from yesterday.
No new stack/cell announcements found from Bloom Energy, FuelCell Energy, Sunfire, SolydEra, Mitsubishi Power, Kyocera, or Aisin in the last 24-48h.

Top story — see Top Signal #1.* Trump-Thune engagement on Senate floor action for a data-center electricity cost bill, against a backdrop of three competing proposals (House Ratepayer Protection Act, Van Hollen's Power for the People Act S.3682, Wyden's excise-tax white paper). Standing background unchanged: PJM backstop reliability auction (bid window Sept 30-Oct 21), FERC co-location transmission-service order in compliance-filing phase, FERC RM26-4 Section 206 show-cause orders (responses due Nov 16), Virginia's $0.011/kWh self-generation tax, US ITC 48E 30% fuel-cell ITC (natural-gas/biogas SOFC now qualifies post-OBBBA), New York's permit moratorium, Texas's development pause, Germany's EnEfG-Novelle (pending) and EEG-Novelle 2027 (first Bundestag reading Sept 24).

McDermott International signs MOU with Doosan Enerbility (South Korean gas/steam turbine and generator supplier) to jointly evaluate power generation projects, explicitly including behind-the-meter generation for data centers — a new entrant into the gas-turbine-for-datacenters competitive set, though no specific project or MW figure disclosed yet. [WWT/DCD coverage via search; primary McDermott/Doosan release not independently verified — flag for follow-up]

Battery storage context (no single new deal, but a relevant competitiveness datapoint): ~10.3 GW / 31 GWh of battery storage came online in H1 2026, up >23% YoY; behind-the-meter data-center battery demand projected to scale from ~5 GWh (2026) to 24.4 GWh (2030). Batteries remain a complement/bridge rather than a baseload substitute for SOFC in most current deployments.

Standing pipeline unchanged: hyperscaler nuclear/SMR commitments >9.8 GW (Microsoft-Constellation TMI, Google-Kairos, Amazon-X-energy, Meta), NNSA-Amentum Savannah River Site lease talks, Oracle-VoltaGrid 2.3 GW gas fleet, Doosan Fuel Cell/HyAxiom ~140 MW PAFC order, Crusoe-Boom Supersonic 1.21 GW gas-turbine order, gas-turbine lead times still ~5-7 years.

Bloom Energy (BE): Mizuho PT raised to $351 from $242 (Outperform reiterated) — see Top Signal #2. S&P 500 formal inclusion effective before Monday Sept 21 open. YTD +222%. Securities class-action lead-plaintiff deadline Sept 28; Q3 earnings Oct 27.

FuelCell Energy (FCEL): Robbins LLP issued a lead-plaintiff-deadline reminder (Sept 18) for the securities class action covering purchasers between June 4-Sept 1, 2026 (the period spanning the Fit Energy agreement disclosures and the Sept 2 stock drop on production-rate/cost-structure concerns, both already logged). No new operational news.
Ceres Power (CWR.L): H1 2026 results due Sept 23 before market open — unchanged.

lcoe.text: Henry Hub outlook: Futures through September 2026 remain below $3.00/MMBtu; EIA expects the spot price to stay below $3.00/MMBtu until November. This is below the model's carried-forward $4.00-4.30/MMBtu assumption and below the Oct-2025-vintage STEO Q3 forecast (~$3.91/MMBtu) — worth reconciling the model's gas-price input against this more recent, lower trajectory. (Last independently confirmed spot print: $2.81/MMBtu, Sept 9.)

Competing gas-turbine capacity keeps adding entrants (McDermott-Doosan Enerbility MOU, above) even as lead times stay stretched ~5-7 years — reinforces SOFC's ~90-day build-time advantage as a differentiator in behind-the-meter bids, a qualitative LCOE-adjacent competitiveness factor rather than a cost figure.

Carry-forward, unchanged: US ITC 48E 30% credit for natural-gas/biogas SOFC (construction start post-Dec 31 2025, domestic-content thresholds 45%/50%/55% in 2026-28); Virginia's $0.011/kWh self-generation tax; PJM's $555/MW-day backstop ceiling.

Pending calendar: Ceres H1 results (Sept 23), Germany EEG-Novelle first Bundestag reading (Sept 24), Bloom formal S&P 500 entry (Sept 21 open), FCEL lead-plaintiff deadline (Sept 18, passed), Bloom lead-plaintiff deadline (Sept 28), PJM backstop bid window (Sept 30-Oct 21), Bloom Q3 earnings (Oct 27).
